findings: Revised definition and experiment plan now cover measurable steady state, hypothesis, control, scoped perturbation, observation, stopping/recovery, and iterative learning. This fixes the earlier mismatch where simulated WireMock errors were presented as Chaos Engineering itself.

Java fence is self-contained for the stated Resilience4j 2.3.0 / JUnit 5 / Java 17+ scope: config, supplier, five failure calls, OPEN assertion, rejected call count invariant, and separate fallback are internally coherent. It demonstrates a local component-level breaker mechanism only; accompanying prose explicitly says it does not test real network, routing, distributed behavior, or full chaos experiment.
“Успех одного опыта не доказывает...” is sound. Automation is phrased as helpful regular feedback, no longer limited to successful experiments.

Hypothesis/control phrasing now tracks the primary Chaos Engineering principles. Minor accuracy nuance: “контроль” is described as determined by experiment conditions; an actual control group is optional depending on experiment design, so avoid implying every experiment needs a literal parallel traffic group.
Related breaker wire-up is pedagogically distinct from system-level chaos; prose makes distinction explicit.

findings: Body now makes strategy a goal/contract/feedback/cost decision and differentiates roles from API names. It explicitly separates Fowler-style Test Spy from Mockito spy and notes Mockito.mock can serve as a stub.

InMemory fake is now scoped: useful for related operations but not SQL/transaction/constraint equivalence; selecting one for every repository is rejected. State/history isolation is not prescribed as a fresh instance in every case.

Tradeoffs preserve practical value: choose stub for controlled answers; interaction verification when it belongs to SUT contract; fake can support outcome assertions; real dependency tests for DB-specific properties.

The question remains defensible at A: “репозиториям — fake” is a heuristic/selection default, not a universal law. The revised body explicitly disclaims automatic selection for every repository, so it narrows and qualifies the shorthand. MCQ edit not required on this basis alone; stronger precision would change A to “для stateful CRUD часто подходит fake”.

B/C/D each make complete, direct strategy claims under the broad stem, not merely isolated facts: B gives a repository replacement rule and cost rationale; C offers a quality heuristic about mock/code ratio; D offers a blanket selection policy and rationale. They occupy narrower subprinciples, but all are actionable answers to “what is the strategy?” No incompleteness finding solely because they are wrong or less comprehensive than A.
No independent SFPL FAIL: this pass was told to assess meaning, and the old option texts remain unchanged. Any form verdict requires a blind structural review; no such claim made.
30.theory_errors: No material factual/strategy error found. One taxonomy nuance: the Fowler/Meszaros link should be checked for exact naming of Test Spy versus mock; current body distinguishes roles clearly enough for study purposes.
